items.q: What is the difference between a chatbot and an AI agent?
items.a: A chatbot answers a message with text. An **agent** works towards a goal in a **loop**: the model decides the next step, the program runs a tool, and the result goes back to the model, until the goal is met or a limit stops it.
items.trap: Saying "an agent is a smarter model". The model can be the same; the loop and the tools make it an agent.

items.q: Does the language model run the tools itself?
items.a: No. The model only returns a **decision** (text or a structured tool request). **Your code** validates it and runs the tool, then sends the result back.
items.trap: Trusting the model's request blindly. Your code is where permissions and checks live.

items.q: Why does every agent loop need a step limit?
items.a: A model can repeat itself or never say "finish". A **max-steps** limit (and often a time or cost limit) stops runaway loops and runaway API bills.
